title: Non-blocking findings from PR #327's review (frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings)
description: Tracked follow-ups for non-blocking findings raised in pr-reviewer's review of PR #327 (frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings) -- one found during the review's own manual browser walkthrough, one corroborated (plus one additional) by the code-review skill run in the background during that same review -- so neither is lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: TradingModeSettingsForm's client-side validation errors (the `errors` state in `TradingModeFields`, frontend/src/features/settings/components/TradingModeSettingsForm.tsx) are only recomputed inside `handleSubmit`, never cleared or re-validated as the user edits a field or toggles the mode radio. Reproduced live: (1) switch to Day Trader mode, type an invalid long-term leg (e.g. 'abc'), click Save -- the format error appears correctly; (2) without clicking Save again, correct the field to a valid value (e.g. '25m') -- the red error border and 'Must be a positive whole number...' helper text remain displayed even though the current field value is now valid, until the user clicks Save again (which re-validates and clears it). The same gap applies to `handleModeChange`: toggling Swing -> Day Trader re-shows the triple fields with whatever stale `errors` were set on the previous attempt, before any new edit or submit. Momentary/cosmetic (the final submitted data is always correctly validated), but misleading mid-edit. Fix: clear (or re-validate) the affected leg's entry in `errors` inside `handleTripleChange`/`handleModeChange` as the user edits, not only inside `handleSubmit`.

`useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess` calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries()` with no filter (frontend/src/features/settings/hooks/useUpdateTradingMode.ts), refetching every mounted query app-wide on every trading-mode save, not just the documented trading-mode-dependent set (stocks/watchlist/portfolio queries). This is a deliberate, already-justified tradeoff (see the parent task's own `decisions` entry and this PR's review notes) rather than an oversight, and isn't blocking -- but worth reconsidering later if this ever causes a noticeable request burst in practice (e.g. once the settings feature or another feature's `queryKeys.ts` registry makes an explicit, maintainable invalidation list cheaper to keep in sync than it is today).

decisions.decision: Fixed the stale-validation-error bug by clearing the edited leg's entry from `errors` inside `handleTripleChange` (delete just that key) and clearing the whole `errors` object inside `handleModeChange`, rather than fully re-validating (recomputing pass/fail) on every keystroke.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item explicitly allows either 'clear (or re-validate)'. A clear-only fix satisfies the reported bug (a corrected value's stale red error/helper text no longer lingers past the edit) without introducing a second behavior change: full live re-validation would also start showing a new error the instant a field goes empty or briefly invalid mid-edit (e.g. typing '2' then '25' then '25m' would flash 'Must be a positive whole number...' after the first two keystrokes), which is more intrusive UX than this bug report asked for and wasn't reproduced/requested as a separate problem. `handleSubmit` already re-validates everything from scratch before calling `mutate()`, so clearing (rather than re-validating) never risks submitting unvalidated data -- only the previous validation pass's cached error is discarded early. Rejected alternative: re-validate the single edited leg's own format on every keystroke (`setErrors(current => ({ ...current, [leg]: validateLeg(...) }))`) -- would also fix the reported bug, but was judged to add exactly the naggy-live-validation downside above for no reporting-required benefit; if a future task wants live inline validation as its own explicit feature, it can build on this clear-first baseline without conflicting with it.

decisions.decision: Implemented a scoped version of the trading-mode invalidation: `useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess` now calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ... })` three times, once per `stocksKeys.all`/`watchlistKeys.all`/`portfolioKeys.all` (a new `all: ['stocks'] as const` was added to `features/stocks/hooks/queryKeys.ts` for this, mirroring the `all` convention `watchlistKeys`/`portfolioKeys` already had), instead of the previous unfiltered `queryClient.invalidateQueries()`. This does not amend the parent task's own already-recorded `decisions` entry (which stays as an accurate record of what was decided and why at that time) -- it supersedes that call for this codebase going forward via this task's own fresh entry.
decisions.rationale: Re-weighed the parent decision's own stated objection (cross-feature import coupling, and silent under-invalidation if a future mode-aware endpoint isn't added to the list) against the actual current codebase state: every other feature's mutation hook (useAddPosition, useAddWatchlistItem, useDeletePosition, useRecordFollowUpReview) already imports its own feature's `queryKeys.ts` and invalidates via its `xKeys.all` prefix constant -- importing three such constants into one settings-feature hook is the same established mechanism used three times, not a new one, and each `xKeys.all` is deliberately documented as a public, shared prefix (each file's own header comment already calls itself 'Shared TanStack Query key conventions'). The 'silently under-invalidate a future mode-aware endpoint' risk is also more contained than the parent decision characterized it: docs/architecture/API.md's own definition of which endpoints depend on trading mode already enumerates only `stocks`/`watchlist`/`portfolio` routes, and any *new* endpoint added under one of those three existing feature namespaces is automatically covered for free by TanStack Query's prefix-matching invalidation (the same 'impossible by construction' argument `portfolioKeys.ts`'s own `risk`/`closedTrades` nesting already relies on) -- the residual risk is narrowed to a hypothetical brand-new *fourth* top-level feature area becoming mode-dependent, which would already require updating API.md's own documented list at the same time, a natural point to also update this invalidation call. Weighed against that narrowed risk: the previous blanket invalidation refetches every mounted query on every mode save, including features API.md never documents as mode-dependent (scanner params, IBKR connection status, daily-homework/trade-journal data) -- a real, avoidable cost on a page whose own settings save is otherwise cheap. Verified via a new unit test (`invalidates only the stocks/watchlist/portfolio query-key prefixes...`, TradingModeSettingsForm.test.tsx) spying on `queryClient.invalidateQueries` directly, asserting exactly the three scoped calls and never an unfiltered one. Rejected alternative: keep the blanket call and only add a decision confirming it (the checklist's other allowed outcome) -- rejected because, on reflection, the coupling cost this task's checklist raised for reconsideration is already paid elsewhere in this codebase for single-feature invalidations, so paying it once more for three already-existing, already-public constants was judged worth the reduced unrelated-refetch cost; also rejected keeping the exact same behavior via three inline literal arrays (`['stocks']`/['watchlist']`/['portfolio']`) instead of importing the constants, since that would silently drift from each feature's own key definition if a feature ever renamed its top-level segment, whereas importing the shared constant can't drift by construction.
